title: Sintsinck (Manhasset Bay)
summary: Sintsinck was recorded for Manhasset Bay or a locality on the bay at Cow Neck, with a separate related use recorded near Hell Gate Neck in Queens.
history_content: A 1639 Dutch record names Sint sinck with Schout's Bay and its dependencies. A separate 1664 Astoria/Hell Gate Neck use of the same form is also recorded, so the public marker is limited to the Manhasset Bay association.
translation_content:
Sintsinck is compared with Ossining/Sing Sing and with interpretations involving stone or a stony place. The precise meaning for the Manhasset Bay use remains uncertain.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names serve as keys to cultural history, to the perception of space by already extinct societies.”

— Peter Jordan, Place Names as ‘Condensed Narratives’ about the Geographical Feature Denoted and the Name-Giving Community (2021), Discussion of cultural-geographical perspective
preservation_content: Sintsinck preserves an older name connected with Manhasset Bay and Cow Neck while also showing how similar recorded forms could appear in more than one colonial land record.
